summary: Demo summary. The instructor explains ordered and unordered lists in Jupyter Notebook Markdown cells, then shows how to insert hyperlinks and images, and asks learners to practise.
keyPoints: Ordered lists use numbering; unordered lists use different symbols (filled circles, filled squares, empty circles) to separate main points from sub-points.
Hyperlinks: display text in square brackets, then the URL in parentheses.
Images use the hyperlink syntax preceded by an exclamation mark (!); the bracket text is shown if the image fails to load.
The same notation can also insert audio, video and other media.
insights: Markdown cells in Jupyter Notebooks let you present information clearly with formatted lists, hyperlinks and embedded media.
Descriptive text inside the brackets of an image ensures alternative text is shown if the image URL is broken or unavailable.
